- Solid cross (colored core, 45/53px single node): the yellow cross was solid at start; after SPACE the blue cross became solid.
- The white core marks the hollow cross.
Wait, but which cross moves? The one I moved with the arrow keys was the yellow cross — initially solid (yellow core), and still movable after SPACE (hollow, white core). So the hollow one (white core) is the movable one! And the solid one (colored core) is… stationary?
Hmm, wait: before SPACE, yellow was solid (yellow core), blue was hollow (white core). I pressed UP (step 1): nothing moved (board_changed? step 1's Ybbox is the same as step 0). Then SPACE (step 2): yellow became hollow (white core), blue became solid (blue core). Then UP×5: yellow moved. So after SPACE, the hollow yellow cross moved.
So the rule is: the hollow cross (white core) is the active/movable one. SPACE toggles which cross is hollow (i.e., switches control between the crosses).
At start: blue was hollow → blue was movable? But my first UP (step 1) didn't move blue… hmm. Wait, step 1: the Ybbox is the same; did blue move? Maybe the game starts with no active cross, and SPACE activates one? First SPACE: yellow became hollow (white core), blue became solid. Then yellow moved. So SPACE made yellow active.

Unless the first UP actually did move blue by 3px and then… no, the arms are identical.

So the state is: exactly one cross is hollow (white core) = active/movable; the other is solid (colored core) = inactive. SPACE toggles.
Now, collection: the yellow cross (when active) collected yellow squares by center overlap. Does the solid cross also collect? Or only the active one?
And the goal: collect all 8 squares? But the off-grid squares are unreachable by center overlap… unless the solid cross can be "pulled" to a different position? No, the solid cross can't move.
Hmm wait, maybe collection isn't center overlap. Let me reconsider: when the yellow cross's center was exactly on top of a square's center, the square's center pixel was absorbed. For (17,15), the center can't be placed there. So (17,15) can never be collected by the yellow cross.
Unless the blue cross can collect it! The blue cross's grid: center (42,36), step 3 → rows ≡ 0 mod 3, cols ≡ 0 mod 3. (17,15): row 17 ≡ 2. This is also unreachable.
So (17,15) is uncollectible by either cross. Same for the blue squares: (16,48) row 16≡1; (24,40) col 40≡1; (24,53) col 53≡2; (35,48) row 35≡2. All unreachable.
So the goal can't be "collect all 8." Maybe the goal is "collect 3 yellow + 3 blue"? But all the blue squares are unreachable! I've only collected 3 yellow so far.
Hmm, so maybe the goal isn't collection at all. Let me think differently.
Maybe the goal is: the crosses need to "swap" positions? Or the crosses need to overlap with each other? Or the crosses need to be placed at specific target locations?
Wait — maybe the squares are targets for the cross's center, and the off-grid ones are… hmm.
Let me look at the geometry again. Yellow squares: (3,15), (9,6), (9,24), (17,15). Blue squares: (16,48), (24,40), (24,53), (35,48).
Yellow cross start: (27,21). Blue cross start: (42,36).

Blue cross start (42,36): blue centroid: ((16+24+24+35)/4, (48+40+53+48)/4) = (24.75, 47.25). No.

The "collection" I observed (center pixel absorbed) might just be a side effect of the cross's center overlapping a square's center — or maybe the squares get "captured" when the arm passes over the center?
But wait, when the yellow cross's vertical arm passed through (17,15), the square wasn't absorbed. Hmm. But maybe absorption only happens when the cross's center is exactly on top of the square's center (a visual effect), and the actual goal is arm alignment.
Or the goal: collect 3 of each color (the reachable ones), and the 4th is… no.
Actually, let me reconsider: maybe when the cross is at (9,15), the arms pass through all 4 yellow squares' centers, and the squares get collected one by one as the arms pass over them? But (17,15) wasn't collected when the arm passed through… unless collection requires the cross to be stationary at the intersection, or requires the arm to pass through in a specific way.
Hmm, let me test: move the yellow cross to (9,15) and observe the squares. Currently at (18,15). UP×3 → (9,15). Then check the state of the squares. If the 4 yellow squares get absorbed/collected (or the level completes), the goal is confirmed.
Actually wait — when the cross was at (15,15) and (18,15), the vertical arm passed through (17,15) and (3,15) (col 15, rows 4-26 / 7-29). The squares at (3,15) and (17,15) — (3,15) was already collected earlier. (17,15) wasn't collected. So arm passage during movement doesn't collect.
Let me test the (9,15) hypothesis: move UP×3 to (9,15) and inspect.
